material.assumptions: Average properties of European-grown Scots Pine; moderate moisture content (~12-15%); uniform cross-section and small vibration amplitude
material.reference: Mederski et al. (2021) - Density and Mechanical Properties of Scots Pine (Pinus sylvestris L.), Drewno Journal

geometry.notes: Heights are measured from the top downward. Diameters correspond to top, ground level, and bottom (buried end).

reference.description: Frequency deviation thresholds used to classify stiffness loss and structural degradation in wooden poles.

sources.authors: Oikawa, D.; Nemoto, S.; Gotou, H.; Aoki, Y.
sources.title: Estimation method of degradation state for timber bridges using vibration analysis
sources.notes: Defines <5%, 5-15%, and >20% natural-frequency drop as minor, moderate, and severe degradation categories.

sources.authors: González de Paz, L. V.; Ortega, N. F.; Rosales, M. B.
sources.title: Assessment of wood utility poles' deterioration through natural frequency measurements
sources.notes: Confirms similar ranges (5-15%, >20%) for decay detection in wooden utility poles.

sources.title: Detection of structural damage through changes in natural frequency: A review
sources.notes: Shows that <5% variation typically corresponds to environmental effects, not structural damage.
